newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU telecoms liberalisation seen boosting jobs.
newsitem.headline: EU telecoms liberalisation seen boosting jobs.

text.p: Speedy liberalisation of the European Union's telecommunications markets could create or maintain up to 1.3 million jobs by 2005, according to a study released on Thursday.

The EU's plan to abolish state telecoms monopolies in most countries by January 1, 1998 could force up to 286,000 workers out of jobs at traditional phone companies, according to the study by French consultants BIPE.
But it could also ensure a net gain of 93,000 jobs in the telecoms sector alone, a European Commission statement summarising the report said.

"There have been and will continue to be job losses in some sectors - particularly in the telecom services provided by traditional operators," EU Employment Commissioner Padraig Flynn said in the statement.
"However, the overall message from this study is upbeat."
The consultants, who began their study in 1994, examined the employment situation in the 15 EU member states over the period 1993-2005.

They found that telecoms liberalisation would create faster diffusion of services and lower prices, boosting the EU economy as a whole. It would also create jobs at new companies that compete with the traditional monopolies.

Most job losses so far have been voluntary, involving unskilled, administrative, network management and maintenance staff, the study found. New jobs have been created in customer management, sales and marketing staff.

Flynn warned, however, that the figures were only forecasts, which are "by their very nature uncertain". In fact, the Commission said publication of the report had been delayed for three months because liberalisation in the EU is moving so quickly that one of the forecasts became obsolete.
